title: Linear algebra: steering a car through space
sub: Vectors, dot products, matrices, rotation, inverse and eigenvectors, all shown on a moving car.

title: A neural network, shown in full
sub: One neuron, a layer, a deep network with every neuron and weight drawn, and how many numbers it learns.

title: How a language model reads and answers
sub: Tokens, numbers, vectors, attention, next-word odds, the tower of layers and the loop that writes a reply.

title: RAG: a library that answers questions
sub: Documents, chunks, the map of meaning, retrieval and the final prompt, with real sentences moving through.

title: Automation: a script that does your Monday report
sub: Find the files, combine them, clean, summarise, save an Excel file and schedule it, with the data moving along a conveyor.

title: Statistics you can see: mean, median, spread and the bell curve
sub: A histogram built from dots, the balance point (mean), the middle (median), an outlier, standard deviation and why sample averages form a bell.

title: Machine learning: a line that learns
sub: Guess a line, measure the mistakes, square them, then let gradient descent fix the line by itself. Finish with scikit-learn.

title: Overfitting: perfect on the past, wrong on the future
sub: The same ten dots fitted with a line, a gentle curve and a wild curve, and why you must test on data the model has never seen.

title: Clustering: finding groups nobody labelled (k-means)
sub: Three centres drop onto 15 customers, every customer joins the nearest one, the centres move to the middle, and again until nothing changes.

title: Decision trees: a game of 20 questions
sub: A loan example: the tree asks the question that best separates approved from rejected, then asks again inside each answer.

title: How a computer sees: convolution, ReLU and pooling
sub: A 3×3 filter slides over an image and lights up where an edge is; ReLU and pooling clean it up; PyTorch stacks it into a CNN.

title: PyTorch: the training loop, step by step
sub: Tensors, a model, a loss, backward, step. The same five lines train a tiny line or a giant network.

title: From text to numbers: tokens, bag of words and n-grams
sub: Cut a sentence into words, count them, line up three sentences in a table, and teach a tiny model to tell happy reviews from angry ones.

title: TF-IDF and cosine similarity: build a search engine
sub: Common words must count less. Weigh the words, turn documents into arrows, measure the angle between them, and rank search results.

title: Embeddings: meaning as geometry
sub: Every word becomes a point in space. Similar meanings sit close together, and arithmetic on the points carries meaning: king − man + woman lands on queen.

title: Characters, bytes and vocabularies
sub: What a letter really is to a computer, how Unicode and UTF-8 store every language and emoji, and why a vocabulary of whole words fails on new words.

title: Byte-Pair Encoding from scratch
sub: Start from single letters, repeatedly glue the most frequent neighbouring pair into a new token, and watch "est" and "low" appear by themselves.

title: Classification: logistic regression and k-nearest neighbours
sub: Two groups of dots, two different ways to draw the line between them, click anywhere to ask a model about a new point, and how to count right and wrong answers.

title: Cross-validation, pipelines and tuning
sub: Test the model five times on five different held-out slices, chain scaling and the model into one pipeline, and let a grid search pick the best settings.

title: KPIs and the metric tree: which number to move
sub: Break revenue into visitors × conversion × order value, find which lever is cheapest, split a monthly change into its causes, and avoid the average-of-rates trap.

title: Funnels: where do people drop out?
sub: Count people at each step from raw events, find the step that leaks most, test what fixing it would be worth, and compare devices.

title: Cohorts: do they come back?
sub: Group customers by the month they joined, count how many are still active a month later, two months later, and read the triangle of numbers as a heat map.

title: Who matters: Pareto and RFM segments
sub: Sort 200 customers by revenue and see how few of them make most of it, then score everyone by Recency, Frequency and Monetary value to find champions and customers at risk.

title: A/B tests: design, sample size and reading the result
sub: Randomise, compare two conversion rates, decide if the gap is luck, measure the power to find a real lift, size the test before running it, and see why peeking cheats.

title: Forecasting: trend, season, baselines and an honest backtest
sub: Split a monthly series into trend, season and noise, test simple baselines before any clever model, split by time instead of at random, and backtest over several periods.

title: HTTP and REST: how programs talk, with a real server
sub: Read a URL, start a tiny real web server, call it with GET and POST, meet 200, 201 and 404, and retry politely when a server is busy.

title: FastAPI: routes, validation and errors
sub: Turn Python functions into web endpoints, let type hints validate the input, return the right status codes and guard a route with a key.

title: Numbers first: load, storage and servers on the back of an envelope
sub: Turn "2 million users" into requests per second, terabytes and a number of servers, in a few lines, before drawing a single box.

title: Caching and sharding: faster reads, bigger data
sub: Keep the popular answers close, evict the stale ones with LRU, spread the data over machines with hashing, and see why a naive modulo breaks when you add one.

title: CI/CD: a pipeline is a graph
sub: Describe a pipeline as steps and dependencies, find what can run in parallel, time it, make a failure stop the release, and guard the deploy.

title: ETL you can safely run twice: idempotent loads, quality gates and retries
sub: Extract, transform, load a few rows; run the job twice and watch the duplicates; fix it with replace-by-day and upserts; block bad data; retry a flaky task; backfill a date range.

title: Monitoring: when the world stops looking like the training data
sub: Compare last quarter with this week, score the shift with PSI and a KS test, see accuracy fall when the rule itself moves, and turn the scores into an alert policy.

title: Docker layers: why the order of your Dockerfile matters
sub: An image is a stack of layers; a layer is reused when its instruction and inputs are unchanged. Simulate the build cache in a few lines and see a 90-second rebuild become 1 second.

title: Show your work: what a good project post looks like
sub: Compare a weak and a strong post of the same project with a checklist you can run in code: a hook, a number, a link and a question, in plain words.

title: What the numbers say: analysing 50,000 posts
sub: Median against mean for skewed likes, which format and hour work, whether length matters, how few posts take most of the likes, and a bootstrap to check a difference is real.

title: Hooks and a weekly content system
sub: Reusable hook patterns, a calendar generated by code, batching to save hours, the compounding of showing up weekly, and a review that tells you what to repeat.

title: Users, jobs and measuring usability
sub: Say what job the user hires the product for, then measure how well it works: the SUS questionnaire score, the success rate with an honest interval, time on task and a ranked list of problems.

title: Layout, contrast and accessibility, with real numbers
sub: Compute the WCAG contrast ratio of two colours, test and fix a failing pair, choose colours that survive colour blindness, and check spacing, type sizes, touch targets and line length.

title: Honest charts and dashboards
sub: See how a cut axis turns a 5% difference into a giant, why two rising lines always seem related, why -50% then +50% is not zero, and how to build tiles and titles that tell the truth.

title: Usability tests and UI experiments
sub: Why five testers find most problems, how to tally a small test, which task to fix first, how big an A/B test of a button must be, and which guardrail metrics stop a "win" from being a loss.

title: Streamlit: the rerun model, widgets, state and caching
sub: See that every click reruns your whole script, test a real Streamlit app without a browser, keep values between runs with session state, cache slow work, and handle empty results.

title: Gradio: a demo page for a model
sub: Wrap a model in a function, give it a web page with Gradio, show users clear errors, let it say "not sure", and think about batching.

title: Shipping a data app: checks before deploy
sub: Pin your requirements, keep secrets out of code, smoke-test the app, do the memory arithmetic of a free host and run a deploy checklist.

title: Niche, portfolio and how many leads you need
sub: Score niches with weights and test whether the ranking survives other weights, check a one-line offer, choose the three portfolio pieces that cover what clients need, and work out how many leads one client costs.

title: Scoping and pricing with real arithmetic
sub: Turn a target income into an hourly rate, build a fixed price from three-point estimates, simulate overruns, see what a discount really costs and price a change request.

title: Invoices, milestones and contracts (an overview)
sub: Add up an invoice without rounding errors, schedule milestone payments, age your unpaid invoices, price lateness, plan cash around real payment times and check a draft contract for missing clauses.

title: Capacity, progress reports and referrals
sub: Check whether a new project fits your weeks, report real progress, forecast a finish date, see why asking for referrals matters, and find the clients that are not worth it.

title: Probability and Bayes: updating what you believe
sub: Why a positive test from a good test can still mean "probably healthy", how to count it with whole people, how belief updates with each new piece of evidence, and how spam filters use the same rule.

title: Right and wrong answers: TP, TN, FP, FN
sub: Sort every prediction into four boxes, compute precision, recall and F1, see why accuracy misleads on rare events, move the threshold, choose it by cost and put an honest interval on a small result.

title: Derivatives: the slope of a curve
sub: Measure a slope by zooming in, check the textbook rules with numbers, get speed from position, use the chain rule and find a minimum where the slope is zero.

title: Integrals, gradients and gradient descent
sub: Add up thin slices to get an area, recover distance from speed, take the gradient of a function of two numbers, walk downhill, see what the learning rate does and fit a line by descent.

title: Tensors and autograd
sub: Make tensors, see how they relate to NumPy arrays, let PyTorch compute a gradient for you, check it by hand, learn why gradients accumulate and when to switch tracking off.

title: Layers, parameters and losses (nn.Module)
sub: Open up a Linear layer, count the parameters of a network, write your own module, check a loss by hand, compare activation functions and see why dropout behaves differently when training.

title: Evaluate, stop early and save
sub: Split the data three ways, watch training and validation loss drift apart, stop at the right moment and keep the best model, then save, load and resume with checks that nothing changed.

title: CNN shapes, receptive fields and cost
sub: Predict the output size of a convolution, count its parameters, grow the field a neuron can see, compare the cost of different stacks and trace the shapes through a whole network.

title: Augmentation and transfer learning
sub: Make more training pictures from the ones you have, learn which changes keep the label true, then reuse what a network learned on one task to learn another from very few examples.

title: Detection and segmentation building blocks
sub: Measure how well two boxes overlap (IoU), count candidate boxes, remove duplicates with non-maximum suppression, score detections with average precision, judge masks with Dice and see how a network gets its image size back.

title: Autoencoders and the latent space
sub: Squeeze 64 pixels into 2 numbers and rebuild the picture, compare with PCA, look at what the 2 numbers mean, walk between two digits, clean noise and meet the KL term of the variational autoencoder.

title: Diffusion, part 1: adding noise
sub: Destroy data with noise on a fixed schedule, jump straight to any noise level with one formula, measure signal against noise, watch two humps melt into one bell and compare noise schedules.

title: Diffusion, part 2: removing noise
sub: Write down the perfect denoiser for two-humped data, run the reverse process from pure noise, take fewer steps, train a small network to do the same job and see where its errors are largest.

title: Guidance and evaluating generators
sub: Steer a diffusion sampler towards a condition and see the price of pushing too hard, then judge generators properly: FID, its small-sample bias, precision and recall, and the memorising trap.

title: Memory, bandwidth and what fits
sub: Count the parameters of a 7-billion-parameter model from its shape, turn them into gigabytes at each precision, add the KV cache, see what fits in 24 GB and why generation speed is set by memory bandwidth.

title: Quantisation
sub: Round weights to a few bits and measure the damage, see how one outlier ruins a whole tensor, fix it with a scale per row or per group, check the effect on a matrix product and count the true cost per weight.

title: Attention and the KV cache
sub: Write attention in six lines, see what the causal mask does, generate with and without a cache and prove the answers match, count the work each way and shrink the cache with shared key-value heads.

title: Batching and speculative decoding
sub: See how waiting for the slowest request wastes the card, how continuous batching fixes it, why throughput rises with the number of conversations, and how a small draft model can let the big one check several words at once.

title: Prompt, retrieve or tune? And the dataset
sub: Decide between a better prompt, retrieval and fine-tuning, then audit the examples you would tune on: duplicates, empty answers, leakage into the test set, balance, how much data helps and how to split.

title: LoRA: tune a tiny adapter, freeze the giant
sub: Count what a low-rank update saves, build a LoRA layer and check it starts as the original, train it against full tuning at several ranks, merge it back and total the savings for a whole model.

title: Quantisation and memory for tuning
sub: Add up what training needs per parameter, compare full tuning, LoRA and QLoRA for a 7B model, build a 4-bit grid shaped for bell-curve weights, save on the scales and see what fits in 24 GB.

title: Evaluate the tuned model honestly
sub: Compare a base and a tuned model on the same 300 questions with a confidence interval and a paired test, size the test set, look for what the tuning broke elsewhere and write the report. The test results are simulated, so that every number can be explained.

title: The agent loop and tool calling
sub: Describe tools a model may call, run the loop of ask, act and observe, feed errors back, stop a model that loops, keep a calculator from running arbitrary code and count what every extra step costs.

title: State graphs: LangGraph in plain Python
sub: Build a small graph engine in 25 lines, run a linear graph, add a loop with a condition, combine updates with reducers, save and resume from checkpoints, pause for a human and check a graph for dead ends.

title: GraphRAG: retrieval over a knowledge graph
sub: Keep knowledge as facts linking entities, see where plain similarity search fails on a question that needs two hops, retrieve by walking the graph, find themes with communities, count the cost of building the graph and compare both ways on four questions.

title: Bandits: explore or exploit
sub: Choose between three options whose payoffs you do not know: pure exploitation gets stuck, a little random exploration helps, a decaying rate helps more, and UCB and Thompson sampling explore on purpose. Simulated over 300 repeated games of 1,000 pulls each.

title: Returns, Q-learning and value iteration
sub: Add up future rewards with a discount, solve a small grid exactly by value iteration, let an agent learn the same thing by trial and error with Q-learning, watch how fast it learns and see how the discount changes behaviour.

title: Policy gradients
sub: Learn the policy itself instead of values: check the gradient formula against a numerical one, run REINFORCE on the bandit, see what a baseline does to the noise and train a grid-walking policy.

title: RLHF and DPO: alignment from preferences
sub: Turn pairs of "which answer is better?" into a reward model, see how a penalty for drifting from the original model shapes the best policy, compute the DPO loss that skips the reward model, train it on a toy and see how optimising a flawed reward backfires.

title: Graphs, confounders and colliders
sub: Draw cause and effect as arrows, watch a confounder fake an effect, see why adjusting for the right variable fixes it and adjusting for the wrong kind of variable breaks it, and learn which to adjust for. All data are simulated with a known truth.

title: Propensity scores and weighting
sub: Estimate each person's chance of being treated, use it to re-weight a lopsided comparison, check that the groups are balanced afterwards, handle extreme weights and see what happens when an important variable is missing. Simulated, with a known effect.

title: Cutoffs and instruments
sub: Two ways to get a causal answer from observational data: compare people just either side of a cutoff, or use an outside nudge (an instrument) that moves the treatment but affects the outcome in no other way. Simulated, with the truth known.

title: Synthetic controls and placebo tests
sub: Measure the effect of something that happened to one unit (a city, a store, a country) by building a weighted blend of similar untouched units as its "what would have happened", and test the result by pretending the same thing happened to the others. Simulated, with the truth known.

title: Images as tokens
sub: Cut a picture into patches, turn each patch into a token with one shared matrix, give every token a position, count how many tokens a picture costs at different sizes and see what pooling throws away.

title: CLIP: aligning images and text
sub: Train two small encoders so that a picture and its caption land close together, measure retrieval and zero-shot classification, vary the temperature and the batch size, and see what a bag-of-words text side cannot do. Built on the 8 × 8 digits, with no pretrained model.

title: Audio, spectrograms and speech accuracy
sub: Turn sound into numbers: sampling and the frequencies a signal can carry, the spectrogram, the mel scale, how many tokens a minute of speech costs, and how word error rate is computed and misread. Real FFTs on synthetic signals.

title: Multimodal pipelines: cost, OCR and latency
sub: Compare the cost of reading a page as text or as an image, see how latency adds up and where the slowest requests come from, follow OCR errors through search, avoid paying twice for the same page and decide when to use which route.

title: From a model to an API
sub: Save a trained model, serve it with a real FastAPI app, load it once, validate every input, report health, and test that the API answers exactly like the model. Runs the real app through its test client.

title: Config, containers and the CI gate
sub: Layer configuration (defaults, file, environment, flags), validate it, make training reproducible and record what went into a model, lint a Dockerfile, gate a release on metrics and promote a model only through a checked, signed-off step.

title: LLMOps: evals, budgets and cost
sub: Work out what a language model feature costs, find where the money goes, cap heavy users, see what a cache and a cheap-model-first router save, gate a prompt change on a proper test and catch a drift in output length. Prices and traffic are assumptions; traffic is simulated.

title: Choosing a problem and proving it works
sub: Pick a project with a transparent score, set the baseline to beat before you build anything, show with an interval that you beat it, learn whether more data would help, look for where the model fails, and write the one-page spec. Uses the breast-cancer data bundled with scikit-learn.

title: A small project, end to end
sub: Do the whole loop once on a small problem: lock a test set away, compare models by cross-validation, tune lightly, choose a threshold on validation data, test once with intervals, and package the model with a manifest and a reload test.

title: Interview drills: SQL, Python and ML
sub: Practise the questions that come up in data interviews, with runnable answers and the reasoning to say out loud: SQL ranking and joins, Python complexity, precision and recall from counts, overfitting, and the two leaks that fool cross-validation.

title: README, resume bullets and your story
sub: Check a README against a checklist, tighten resume bullets, time a 90-second pitch, test the structure of a project story, verify that every number in your README exists in your results file, and run a last checklist before you share.

title: The command line: files, pipes and environment variables
sub: Work in folders by path, filter text with small tools joined by pipes, send output and errors to files, pass settings through environment variables and read exit codes. Every idea is run for real on a temporary folder.

title: Git: history, branches, merges and mistakes
sub: Commit, branch and merge in a real repository built on the spot, resolve a conflict, undo mistakes with revert and reset, see why a deleted secret is still in history, and find the commit that broke something with bisect.

title: Reproducible projects: virtual environments and requirements.txt
sub: Build a real virtual environment, prove it is separate from the main Python, check a requirements file against what is installed, compare versions the way pip does, and fingerprint a requirements file.

title: Kubernetes: desired state and the reconcile loop
sub: Understand Kubernetes by building its core ideas in a few lines: a reconcile loop, crash back-off, rolling updates with surge and unavailable limits, probes, autoscaling by formula and packing pods onto nodes.

title: Infrastructure as code
sub: Describe servers and networks in a file instead of clicking: compute a plan of what would change, apply it twice and see nothing happen the second time, detect drift, order resources by their dependencies and keep secrets out of reach.

title: Observability: percentiles, SLOs and error budgets
sub: Measure latency the right way: percentiles instead of averages, error budgets in minutes, burn-rate alerts that page for real incidents and ignore blips, the error hidden in histogram buckets, why p99s cannot be averaged, and the cost of high-cardinality labels.

title: dbt-style models and tests
sub: Build a tiny dbt in Python and SQLite: models that refer to each other with ref(), a build order worked out from those references, tests that catch bad data, incremental loads and impact analysis.

title: MapReduce, Spark ideas and data contracts
sub: Count words the MapReduce way, see how keys are split across reducers, cut network traffic with a combiner, tame a hot key by salting, understand lazy evaluation and lineage, and check data against a contract.

title: Rate limits, retries and queues
sub: Limit traffic with a token bucket, see why fixed windows leak bursts, spread retries with jitter, watch queues explode near full load, make retries safe with idempotency keys and park hopeless jobs in a dead-letter queue.

title: Designing ML and RAG systems with numbers
sub: Do the arithmetic of an AI product: memory for millions of embeddings, exact against approximate nearest-neighbour search with measured recall, a latency budget, cache savings and a fallback ladder with its availability.

title: HTML is a tree: parse it and select from it
sub: See a web page as a tree of nested tags, read it with a parser and with BeautifulSoup, pick elements with CSS selectors and XPath, write selectors that survive a redesign, and see how parsers treat broken HTML.

title: Extract and clean what you found
sub: Turn scraped strings into numbers and dates: clean whitespace and entities, parse prices with different symbols and separators, parse dates and spot the day-first trap, read an HTML table, deduplicate and validate with a quarantine.

title: APIs, pagination and retries
sub: Read JSON from an API, crawl every page, see how offset paging repeats items while a cursor does not, tell retryable errors from permanent ones, retry with back-off and jitter, handle timeouts and resume a crawl after a crash.

title: Being polite, legal and accurate
sub: Read robots.txt, keep to a crawl delay, identify your bot, save bandwidth with conditional requests and a cache, and think through what is allowed. The servers used are local ones started by the lesson.

title: Django models and the ORM, as a working miniature
sub: See how a class becomes a table, how filter builds SQL lazily, how a foreign key works, why one query per row (N+1) is slow and select_related fixes it, and how migrations and transactions protect data. Built as a miniature, because Django itself is not installed here.

title: Django URLs, views and templates, as a working miniature
sub: Build a URL router with typed parts, views that return responses and status codes, a small template engine with automatic escaping, a middleware chain, and a test client that checks it all. A miniature, since Django is not installed here.

title: Telling the truth with numbers
sub: Six ways true numbers mislead, each run on real or simulated data: Simpson's paradox, percent against percentage points and base rates, the mean against the median, many comparisons, survivorship, and picking the best window.

title: Causal thinking: when you cannot randomise
sub: Estimate the effect of a change you could not randomise: difference in differences with a parallel-trends check, a placebo test, propensity weighting and matching, and how strong a hidden confounder must be to explain the result away. All on simulated data with a known true effect.

title: Recommenders and ranking metrics
sub: Measure a ranked list properly (precision, recall, average precision, NDCG, MRR), evaluate recommenders on the future, compare popularity, item-based and matrix-factorisation methods, look beyond accuracy, and meet cold start and position bias.
